title_vi: Cookie và session khác nhau thế nào?

source_snapshot.note: Pinned commit/path body independently hashed as Git blob; computed OID matches provider tree OID. Non-empty source was read; no source-image bytes used.

claims.evidence: MDN's HTTP cookies guide read from a local clone; session behaviour observed with a small Python server and curl.

mobile.evidence: Chromium (Playwright) rendered the full lesson at each width with optional sections open; diagram scale measured from the rendered image and every SVG text box checked against the viewBox. Not learner testing and not GitHub or a real phone.

claims.claim_vi: The source says cookies and sessions both carry user information such as login status across HTTP requests; cookies are small (about 4KB), stored on the user's device and sent with each subsequent request; a session is created and stored on the server, a unique session ID is returned in a cookie, sessions can hold more data and are described as offering more security.

A server sends a cookie in a Set-Cookie header and the browser sends it back in a Cookie header on later requests; browsers limit each cookie to usually 4KB; by default cookie values are visible to, and can be changed by, the end user; the guide advises regenerating and resending session cookies whenever a user authenticates to help prevent session fixation.
claims.section: Introduction; Limitations; Security; Define the lifetime of a cookie
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of the repository.

claims.claim_vi: With a Python server holding a session dictionary and handing out a random id in an HttpOnly cookie: a request with the right id returned the stored session data; a tampered id returned no data; a request with no cookie returned no data.
claims.verified_by: No external page reports this output; observed by executing the code on the authoring machine. MDN describes the Set-Cookie/Cookie flow but not this output.

claims.claim_vi: A session id is still a secret: whoever obtains the right id can use the session, so session security concentrates in keeping the id secret, and the id cookie should carry HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite.
claims.verified_by: MDN advises these attributes for cookies that carry session identifiers; that session security concentrates in the id is the author's inference.

claims.claim_vi: With data stored on the server, the server has to store and clean up sessions, and several servers need a shared place to keep them.
claims.verified_by: Author's general knowledge; the source only says sessions are stored on the server and can hold more data.

design_notes_vi: Một thẻ nêu lý do, hai nhánh cookie và session theo nơi lưu dữ liệu, thẻ cuối nói hệ quả (mã sai và mã bị lộ). Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: Source says sessions are more secure because data is not accessed directly by the client; the lesson narrows that to the data itself and adds that the session id remains a secret, citing MDN's session-fixation advice.
Source says users 'can choose to ban cookies'; the lesson does not repeat it (unchecked and not needed for the distinction).
editorial_note_vi: Bài mới viết trong kho này, chờ review kỹ thuật. Chưa user testing hoặc phê duyệt phát hành.
